items: The heatmap's colour key is now in your language too.
Dates now read year first, like 2026-11-21, the same in every app. If you prefer your region's style, choose "Dates: Regional" once under the font picker.

Your race calendar can keep itself up to date: a new cowork channel reads your race emails and each race's website for entries, bibs, waves, start times, changes and chip times, and you tick what to apply. It only adds races you have entered. On the Races page you can also ask it to scout for races near you; those are suggestions until you add one.

The analysis pages are in all 16 languages now: Efficiency, Insights, Power, Response, Records, Career, Vitals, Second opinion, Year in review, Durability, Climbing, Experiments and Strength, plus the race plan, fuelling and race review notes.

Races, the race plan, Calendar, Achievements, Plan of the day, Ask & coach, Track & intervals, Replay, share cards, the Journal and My routes are now in all 16 languages, with dates and weekdays written your way.
The analysis speaks your language too: readiness advice, zone and pace names, weather, running-form notes, achievements, and why a run slowed or stopped. What the AI coach reads stays in English.
Today, the Activities list and each activity page are now in all 16 languages too, with dates written your way.

Run315 starts speaking your language: the menus, tab bar and the Sync & cowork page are now in French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Croatian, German, Chinese, Ukrainian, Esperanto, Swahili, Hindi, Bengali, Indonesian, Urdu, Farsi and Arabic (machine translated from English; pick yours under the font settings). Arabic, Farsi and Urdu lay out right to left. The rest of the app follows page by page.

Fifteen colour themes, the same in every app by this maker (Midnight, Ocean, Forest, Ember, Paper, High contrast and more): pick one under Sync & cowork. A light or dark choice you made before carries over.
Tighter security: the app now only talks to the services it needs (Google Drive, the map tiles, weather and place lookups, and Anthropic if you saved a key).

New cowork channel, run-review: an AI grades each finished run or ride against what it was for (easy, long, tempo, intervals, race), using the app's own numbers, your splits, the night before and your journal. You review each grade before it is kept; it then shows on the activity page beside the app's numbers, and can be undone.
While Google Drive sync is on, your Google picture now sits at the top of the app on every screen, so you can always see which account is syncing. Tap it to open the sync settings.

Cowork replies now wait for your review before they change anything: Garmin and Strava imports are listed by part (activities, days and nights, gear) so you can tick what to take, and every applied reply can be undone from the run log. Untick a channel under Sync & cowork to let it apply automatically.
Your Google profile picture shows beside your account when Drive sync is on.
Maps, the SQL console and the AI coach no longer load code from other websites.
Erase everything on this device now removes all of Run315's data and only Run315's, disconnects Drive, and leaves your Drive copy untouched.
Days are always your local day: a late-evening run no longer shows up as tomorrow in charts, the coach's week or air quality.
Atkinson Hyperlegible is the default font, and you can pick another one in Sync & cowork.
Fixed a blank page that could appear right after an update.
Drive sync no longer tries to open a blocked sign-in popup in the background: press Sync now to reconnect when it asks.
Errors are recorded on this device and shown under Sync & cowork, ready to copy into a bug report.
The cowork folder gets a recent.json with your last six weeks, so daily and weekly briefs read fast and can tell when the data is stale.
If the browser forgets the cowork folder after a restart, a button asks for access again instead of exports stopping quietly.
Records and collections, a year in review, shareable images with privacy zones, and air quality on each run.
Replay a run, race your own ghost, and watch your coverage grow in a time-lapse.
Plan a run through streets and tiles you have never covered, and export it as GPX.
W′ balance through a run, and DFA-a1 when your watch records beat-to-beat intervals.
